root_cause_label: Agent abandoned the required stable_kmeans.py in favor of auxiliary files with non-compliant names after failing to resolve a venv/sklearn dependency mismatch
one_sentence_failure_summary: When unable to install sklearn into the active venv, the agent created functionally correct implementations in wrongly-named files (stable_kmeans_simple.py, stable_kmeans_optimized.py) instead of rewriting stable_kmeans.py to be dependency-free or fixing the environment, causing the evaluator to find no StableKMeans class in the required path.
t_err_evidence: At step 29 the agent creates /app/stable_kmeans_simple.py containing a new StableKMeans class, definitively abandoning the task-required /app/stable_kmeans.py instead of fixing its dependency issues or rewriting it with a pure-NumPy implementation.
t_commit_evidence: From step 29 onward the agent directs all effort to auxiliary files (stable_kmeans_simple.py, stable_kmeans_optimized.py, demo scripts, README) and never modifies stable_kmeans.py again, locking in the wrong-file-path outcome.
trigger_explanation: The active Python 3.12 venv had no pip and no sklearn; the agent spent steps 4-26 in repeated failed attempts to install sklearn. Instead of the correct response (rewrite stable_kmeans.py using only NumPy and math, or properly bootstrap pip in the venv), the agent created a new file with a non-compliant name, permanently bypassing the required output path.
forewarning_evidence: Steps 4 and 6 show the same ModuleNotFoundError for sklearn when importing stable_kmeans; steps 8-25 show repeated failed pip/apt installation attempts all targeting wrong interpreters, signaling the environment issue was unresolved before the decisive file-creation pivot at step 29.
